title: High-Order Pointwise CATE Estimation under an Unknown Rough Design Density
banked_reason: D0.5 kernel_substituted@thm:matched-rough-design-rate: unmatched bracket does not prove the promised same-class minimax rate.
gap_reasons: The requested same-class minimax theorem with one deterministic rate is replaced by an explicitly unmatched n^{-1/3}--n^{-3/10} bracket; complete a matching converse (or revise the delivered claim and positioning to the bracket as the actual contribution).

The endpoints n^{-1/3} and n^{-3/10} do not match, and the n^{-22/73} benchmark lies between them; exact benchmark attainability and the sharp rough-design rate remain unresolved.
proof_attempt_summary: The run developed an explicit density-free upper-bound architecture and a legal same-class lower witness, yielding only an unmatched n^{-1/3} to n^{-3/10} risk bracket. A bounded finite-cutoff adaptation for the stronger converse failed to establish positive normalized priors with the required cancellation and the global fixed-n mixture comparison; D0.5 also found a block-count normalization inconsistency in the upper proof. The matched minimax rate and even attainability of the supplied uniform benchmark remain open; the field-tier kernel cannot be claimed from this draft.
tldr: For the fixed eight-dimensional Bernoulli CATE model with an unknown bounded measurable design density, a total finite density-free estimator attains risk \(Cn^{-3/10}\).  A direct pair of legal causal laws in the same class proves \(R_n\ge c n^{-1/3}\), so the rigorous result is the unmatched bracket \(c n^{-1/3}\le R_n\le Cn^{-3/10}\).  The required finite-cutoff lower-bound attempt fails at a concrete normalization equation: cancellation for an unnormalized positive density does not survive division by its random mass, even when the two mass marginals agree and a common Poisson tilt is used.  The supplied \(n^{-22/73}\) benchmark lies between the proved endpoints, so its attainability remains unresolved.
gap: The closest pointwise CATE theorem requires accurate design-distribution estimation for its upper bound, while the closest rough-design theorem concerns constant conditional variance and does not give a constant-factor differentiable-regime converse.
fill: A finite interpolation contrast supplies a density-free upper bound, and a common-density-marginal two-prior construction supplies the legal fixed-\(n\) converse on exactly the same causal class.
